children: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade goes live in October, replacing the network's consensus layer with a new protocol architecture.

The change targets the process Solana uses to reach agreement on the state of its network. Replacing the consensus layer makes the upgrade a broad protocol change rather than a routine software release. The announced timing gives developers and users a defined month for the transition.

If delivered as described, the upgrade could improve finality and performance, affecting how the network is assessed for applications that depend on confirmation speed and reliable processing. Replacing the consensus layer also gives the release wider technical scope than an incremental update. The available description does not provide target figures or implementation details, so the practical effect will depend on how the new layer performs after launch.
